ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee (no refund); no account flag. Optionally note the record inconsistency between F6 and F7 for data-quality follow-up.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider treats 181 m as proof the driver was 'not at the pick-up location', but no clause publishes a pin-exact or metre test for NS-1(ii) [RD-NS-1]; the 200 m radius is a data-layer parameter (gap G2), and the system record shows the driver inside that recorded range at the tap and throughout [F2][F6], so the position limb passes.

The retreat to 181 m and stationary hold [F3] is a position-and-duration fact that satisfies NS-1(iii) rather than defeating it: the driver remained inside the recorded pick-up range for 3 min 40 s after the tap [F6][F2], more than the 3:01 required by NS-1 [RD-NS-1].

NS-2 only bites where an NS-1 limb fails [RD-NS-2]; all three limbs are met on the system record — tap at 14:07:40 [F6], inside range at that moment [F1][F6], and over 3 minutes of waiting after it [F6][F2] — so no full refund of $6.61 arises.

The rider being reachable at the entrance [F11] does not displace NS-1: the driver gave his waiting position at 14:07 [F10] and cancelled only after the wait threshold had elapsed [F12][F4], which is the NS-1 scenario, not NS-2 [RD-NS-1][RD-NS-2].

Correct as stated but immaterial: profile facts never decide the case, and the driver's clean history [F18] neither establishes nor defeats the fee, which turns on the NS-1 records, not on RD-6 [RD-RD-6].

RD-4 governs justification for a reroute and is not a condition of NS-1 [RD-RD-4]; the absence of incidents, speed bands and rain [F14][F15][F16] simply means no exemption or excuse is in issue, leaving the NS-1 analysis undisturbed.

The driver's point that $6.61 with no surge [F8][F9] is the published amount is factually true but not decisive by itself; the fee stands because NS-1 is satisfied [RD-NS-1], not because the figure matches the tariff.

The rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days [F17] cannot be used to establish this breach; profile facts are relevant only to an ancillary account action and never decide the main finding [RD-RD-6].
